ops.title: Upstream cc-transcript: preserve subshell/group boundaries in occurrence walk
ops.description: cc-transcript 14.0 parses `(cd /x) && rm -rf .` identically to `cd /x && rm -rf .` — the subshell parens are stripped and the inner `cd` becomes an ordinary occurrence with `.piped=False`, so a consumer walking occurrences to thread cwd cannot tell the cd runs in a subshell (where its cwd change does NOT persist to the parent shell). The rm-guard's cwd threading (captain_hook/primitives/commands.py visit_handler + packs/general/deletions.py descend_rm) therefore mis-resolves a later relative rm after a subshell cd. Pipeline `cd | rm` IS detectable (`.piped`) and was fixed 2026-07-18; the subshell case needs an Occurrence-level subshell/group flag (or preserved grouping) from cc-transcript. Refuter finding #2 (rm-guard wave 2). Bounded: contrived pattern, not a plausible accident; noted, not blocking.
